newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus guards detain Russian TV crew.
newsitem.headline: Belarus guards detain Russian TV crew.

text.p: Belarussian border guards have detained journalists working for Russian television, accusing them of attempting to cross a border illegally, and said on Sunday one of them could face up to five years in prison.

Dmitry Novozhylov, an administrator for Russian Public Television (ORT ) in Minsk, said he was told by border guards that the company's reporter Pavel Sheremet and his driver were detained late on Saturday at Minsk airport.

"They were arrested by border guards," Novozhylov told Reuters. "Criminal procedings were launched on the grounds, according to the border guards, of an attempt to cross the (Belarussian) border with Lithuania illegally."
Belarus border guards' chief Alexander Pavlovsky told national television that Sheremet's actions were punishable under the former Soviet republic's criminal code.
He did not give any details of the incident in which Seremet and his driver were involved.
"Pavel Sheremet may get up to five years in prison under article 81 which includes punishment for illegal crossing of the border," Pavlovsky said.
ORT cameraman Dmitry Zavadsky was arrested at his home in Minsk on Saturday, Novozhylov added, saying all three ORT employees were being held near the Lithuanian border.

Sheremet was accused by the Belarussian authorities of biased reporting earlier this month and stripped of his foreign ministry media accreditation. Earlier this year, Belarus expelled a reporter for Russia's NTV television.
Liberals in the Russian government, which has forged close links with authoritarian Belarussian President Alexander Lukashenko, criticised Minsk's earlier sanctions on Sheremet.
Novozhylov said the reporter and his crew were filming last week near the Belarussian-Lithuanian border.

Lukashenko, who has been criticised in the West for his attitute to opposition, has closed some Belarussian newspapers down and ousted the editors of others. Some opposition newspapers are now published in Lithuania.
